name: Operation Iron Veil
tagline: The town never paid the piper. We did.
summary: A single-player, first-person story shooter set in an alternate history of the Second World War. A telephone technician from Hameln against the man who planned his city's darkest night.
description: Hameln, 1938. In a Germany where a different regime, the National Renewal Front, took power, telephone technician Paul Hartmann only wants to repair his lines and keep his family together. But Viktor Falkenberg, the regime's brilliant planner and once his father's comrade in arms, is building a plan called the Iron Veil, and Hameln is part of it.

seo.title: Operation Iron Veil – Story-driven first-person game
seo.description: Operation Iron Veil is a single-player first-person story shooter in an alternate history of the Second World War, in development at Jonaz Productions.

hero.headline: Operation Iron Veil
hero.quote: The town didn't pay the piper back then. We paid. Now we play our own tune.

sections.title: A city out of a picture book.
sections.body:
Hameln lies on the Weser: half-timbered houses, sandstone façades, the radio mast on the Klüt above the old town. Paul Hartmann, 24, works for the telephone exchange. He lives above his mother Anna's tailor shop with his brother Lukas and his little sister Mia, who loves the legend of the Pied Piper and plays the recorder.

In this version of history the National Renewal Front rules Germany. In August 1939 it signs an alliance with the Soviet Union. Viktor Falkenberg, the head of the Reich Office for Strategic Planning, designed that treaty, and he never meant to keep it. His plan, the Iron Veil, needs a people ready for total war, and a wound to drive them there.

On the night of 23 October 1940, the air-raid siren in Hameln sounds too late.

Paul's road leads from the burning old town through Hannover to the river Bug, through the Russian winter, into the chalk cellars of Champagne and beneath the streets of London, and finally home again, to the mountain of Weserstein and the man who calculated the price of Hameln.

items.name: Paul Hartmann
items.text: Telephone technician from Hameln. Not a soldier by choice and never a super-soldier: his strongest tools are wires, switchboards and radios.

items.name: Anna Hartmann
items.text: Runs her own tailor's shop on the Wendenstraße and holds the family together. The little melody she hums for her children runs through the whole game.

items.name: Lukas Hartmann
items.text: Apprentice car mechanic, stronger and louder than Paul, and drawn to the regime's promises. The road Paul could have taken.

items.name: Mia Hartmann
items.text: Loves the legend of the Pied Piper, plays the recorder and wins a tin figure of the Piper. The reason behind Paul's decisions.

items.name: Viktor Falkenberg
items.text: Head of the Reich Office for Strategic Planning and architect of the Iron Veil. Cultivated, quiet, never raises his voice, and remembers the names of your children.

sections.title: Grounded, vulnerable, human.
sections.intro: These systems are fully specified in the design documents. They are planned features: nothing is playable yet.

items.title: Grounded first-person combat
items.text: Cover and leaning, grenades, melee, wounds that matter, and allies who fight beside you.

items.title: Stealth
items.text: Sight and sound, hiding, distractions (including technical ones), dogs, disguises.

items.title: Technical mini-games
items.text: Paul's trade: trace and solder lines, patch switchboards, find frequencies, reroute circuits, eavesdrop on conversations.

items.title: Traces
items.text: Your choices change side characters, letters and the epilogue, but never the core story.

items.title: Exploration
items.text: Semi-open areas, optional conversations and around 255 archive entries: documents, photos, letters and radio recordings.

items.title: Four difficulty levels
items.text: Story, Normal, Hard and Realistic. Every level tells the same story.

items.title: Leitmotifs
items.text: Nine musical motifs, a dynamic score and Anna's song as the family theme.

items.title: Accessibility
items.text: Subtitles with speaker colours and sound captions, colour-blind modes, reduced camera shake, remappable keys.
